evidence.quote: I want to come out of it with the cutover shape actually decided, because the steering group asks again on Thursday

observations.why: Tanya frames the goal of the meeting looking forward to Thursday's steering group session with specific concrete constraints.

evidence.quote: Northgate is the smallest and the cleanest, Clyde is the one nobody wants to touch.

observations.why: Tina describes the actual current state of the four specific sites.

evidence.quote: We do this one site at a time. A site goes live, it soaks, and only when that soak is clean do we start the next one.

observations.why: Tanya lays down the general procedural sequence and operating policy for cutovers.

evidence.quote: that's the thing the desk supervisor has been shouting about since June.

observations.why: Xavier describes the concrete operational status quo and historical complaint regarding the shared dispatch desk.

evidence.quote: Running two systems at one desk for a few weeks is a known, contained pain with a named owner. Two cutovers landing in the same week is an unbounded one

observations.why: Tanya evaluates the trade-off at an abstract, categorical level between contained and unbounded risk.

evidence.quote: The soak is two full weeks. That's the Dockside number, and I'd hold us to it.

observations.why: Tina sets a specific future operational duration rule based on past precedent.

evidence.quote: Dockside pilot, back in the spring. We watched the exception queue after go-live and it didn't flatten out until day nine or ten.

observations.why: Tina provides concrete historical observation of the Dockside pilot exception queue.

evidence.quote: Reporting on top of that is what took Dockside down for forty minutes.

observations.why: Xavier recalls the factual historical incident where reporting took Dockside down.

evidence.quote: during cutover, every reporting read comes off the replica. Not "should", not "where possible" — reporting does not touch the live system during a cutover window, full stop.

observations.why: Xavier proposes a strict operational rule governing cutover windows.

evidence.quote: Somewhere between thirty seconds and four minutes depending on the migration job. So a reporting number can be four minutes stale during a cutover.

observations.why: Xavier evaluates the concrete quantitative impact of replica lag.

evidence.quote: Xavier, write it into the runbook as a rule and not as guidance

observations.why: Tanya gives a directive for future documentation in the runbook.

evidence.quote: The vendor stays the system of record for reference data until the last site is live. Every site reads from the vendor's copy, we mirror it read-only, and we take ownership on the day Clyde goes green

observations.why: Xavier details the future phased plan for reference data cutover through the Clyde go-live.

evidence.quote: Keeping one source of truth through the whole programme is worth more than getting ownership early.

observations.why: Xavier invokes an overarching abstract principle for the programme's data integrity.

evidence.quote: So Thursday I'm telling them: one site at a time, two-week soak between sites, reporting off the replica during cutover, vendor holds reference data until Clyde is green.

observations.why: Tanya summarizes the four concrete decisions to be presented on Thursday.
